title: AES Bloc Summons Nigerian Envoy Over Tinubu's Sahel Insecurity Remarks
detail: Burkina Faso Foreign Minister Karamoko Jean-Marie Traoré, speaking on behalf of the Alliance of Sahel States (Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger), summoned Nigeria's chargé d'affaires in Ouagadougou on August 6, 2026 to express 'profound regret' over remarks made by Nigerian President Bola Tinubu on July 30, who attributed worsening Nigerian insecurity partly to a security 'collapse' in Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger. The AES statement, escalating into wider regional media coverage by August 8, called for 'a more accurate presentation of the security context' rather than blaming neighbors, warned of risk to 'frustrations between peoples bound by history, geography and brotherhood,' and called the remarks disrespectful of 'the sacrifice made by the Nigerien army against Boko Haram for years.' Nigeria's embassy pledged to relay the message to Abuja. The episode illustrates AES sensitivity to being framed as a regional security liability even as JNIM/ISSP violence intensified across the confederation during July.
